details: Federal regulators, including FinCEN and the Federal Reserve, have proposed new rules requiring stablecoin issuers to implement bank-style identity checks (KYC) for their direct customers. Crucially, the proposal also clarifies that ordinary users can continue peer-to-peer (P2P) stablecoin transfers on secondary markets without issuers needing to collect personal information on every transaction. This move aims to integrate stablecoins into existing anti-money laundering (AML) frameworks while avoiding an overly draconian approach to individual users.
title: US Regulators Clarify Stablecoin KYC Rules, Preserve P2P Transfers

details: Bitcoin (BTC) is currently trading around $64,000, showing a modest rebound of approximately 0.3-1.6% over the last 24 hours. Despite this slight recovery, market sentiment remains mixed. There's institutional interest from Japan and new ETF proposals from Franklin Templeton, but these are counteracted by continued significant outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs and broader macroeconomic concerns, including a hawkish stance from the Federal Reserve. Some analysts also note that BTC traded below its estimated average production cost on June 20, which could impact miner behavior.
title: Bitcoin Trades Near $64K Amid Mixed Signals and Persistent ETF Outflows

details: The Ethereum Foundation is undergoing significant restructuring, including spending cuts, a revised treasury strategy, and a wave of leadership departures, including co-executive director Hsiao-Wei Wang. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin indicated the foundation would become a "smaller ship." A former contributor warned that Ethereum's core development ecosystem could face a "funding crisis" within nine months, requiring about $30 million annually to maintain secure feature delivery and address long-term challenges. The ETH/BTC ratio has also hit early-2023 lows, suggesting underperformance relative to Bitcoin.
title: Ethereum Foundation Faces Restructuring and Funding Concerns

details: Coinbase announced plans to launch tokenized U.S. stocks for its non-U.S. customers next month. These tokens will be backed 1:1 by traditional equities and will reportedly carry full shareholder rights and dividend payouts. This initiative marks a significant step towards the convergence of traditional finance and crypto infrastructure, allowing for increased accessibility and utility of traditional assets within the blockchain ecosystem.
title: Coinbase to Launch Tokenized US Stocks for Non-US Customers

details: The Illinois legislature has passed a bill, SB 3019, which introduces a 0.2% privilege tax on digital asset transactions. This measure, expected to be signed by Governor JB Pritzker, would require digital asset brokers to register with the Department of Revenue by January 1, 2027. This marks the first such tax in the United States and applies to transactions where the customer is physically present in Illinois or where data indicates Illinois as their primary use location.
title: Illinois Introduces New 0.2% Privilege Tax on Crypto Transactions

details: The notorious MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) bot "JaredFromSubway" was reportedly drained of approximately $7.5 million in a counter-MEV "honeypot" attack. Blockchain monitoring data indicates that the attacker transferred 1,000 ETH to Tornado Cash after swapping stolen WETH, USDC, and USDT for 4,400 ETH. This incident highlights ongoing security vulnerabilities and the risks associated with sophisticated on-chain arbitrage strategies in the crypto ecosystem.
title: MEV Bot "JaredFromSubway" Drained for $7.5 Million in Honeypot Attack
